cues.zh: 几百名科学家齐聚一堂

cues.en: So please join me in welcoming Doctor. Sean Carroll for this evening's talk.
cues.zh: 请和我一起欢迎Sean Carroll博士，为我们带来今晚的演讲。

cues.en: Thanks. It's very very good to be back here at Fermilab where I've spent many many hours of my life in one of the best places to do physics and think about physics,
cues.zh: 谢谢。很高兴再次来到Fermilab。我的人生中有很多时间都在这里度过，这里是世界上最适合做物理学研究和思考物理学的地方之一，

cues.en: in the world. And as I was just talking,
cues.zh: 正如我刚才

cues.en: earlier to some of the Fermilab folks, they said that, you know, many of their public talks are not about particle physics. They just use them as an excuse to talk about all sorts of fun things in science.
cues.zh: 和几位Fermilab的同事交流时，他们说，很多面向公众的演讲并不涉及粒子物理学。他们只是借此机会聊聊科学中各种有趣的话题。

cues.en: And I know that nevertheless half of the audience is particle physicists because of the big meeting here. So this might be the most, demanding public audience talk public talk audience I have ever actually had the pleasure to speak in front of.
cues.zh: 我知道，不过由于这里正在举行大型会议，听众中有一半是粒子物理学家。所以，这可能是我有幸面对过的、要求最高的公众演讲听众了。

cues.en: But I have the benefit of having good stuff to talk about.
cues.zh: 但好在，我有很多值得讲的内容。

cues.en: Particles, fields and the future of physics. Particles, you know what that is. You know what the future of physics is. Secretly,
cues.zh: 粒子、场，以及物理学的未来。粒子嘛，你们知道那是什么。物理学的未来，你们也知道。其实，

cues.en: my hidden agenda that you can't get away from because you're here now is to do quantum field theory.
cues.zh: 我藏在心里的真正 agenda，你们既然来了就躲不开，那就是量子场论。

cues.en: That's what I really want to teach you tonight. So I'm very glad that Fermilab is giving me these six hours, to really
cues.zh: 这才是我今晚真正想教给你们的东西。所以我很高兴 Fermilab 给我六个小时，来真正

cues.en: give you enough
cues.zh: 让你们充分

cues.en: of a taste of what Quantum Field Theory is really all about. So I was lucky enough last July
cues.zh: 领略量子场论究竟是什么。去年七月，我有幸

cues.en: to be spending my Independence Day in Geneva, Switzerland at CERN
cues.zh: 在瑞士日内瓦的 CERN 度过美国独立日，

cues.en: where, it was a rock concert like atmosphere.
cues.zh: 当时的气氛就像一场摇滚音乐会。

cues.en: There was this event. It was planned.
cues.zh: 有这么一场活动，而且是早有安排的。

cues.en: The announcement went out. People lined up. People camped out overnight literally. It looks like a... Like people camping out before a rock concert except there are a lot more Macintosh laptops in the audience than otherwise.
cues.zh: 公告发布后，人们排起了队，甚至真的有人彻夜露营。看起来就像摇滚音乐会前的露营，只不过观众中 MacBook 多得多。

cues.en: And there was no rock concert the next day. There were two PowerPoint presentations.
cues.zh: 第二天没有摇滚音乐会，只有两场 PowerPoint 演示。

cues.en: What in the world would be the content of a PowerPoint presentation that would be good enough that would make people camp out overnight? Well, of course, this was the announcement of the discovery of what we now know as the Higgs boson,
cues.zh: 究竟什么样的 PowerPoint 演示，值得人们彻夜露营？当然，这是宣布发现我们现在所知的希格斯玻色子，

cues.en: a particle,
cues.zh: 一种粒子，

cues.en: that physicists have been looking for for literally decades.
cues.zh: 物理学家足足寻找了几十年的粒子。

cues.en: And we were finally able through thousands of people working together, billions of dollars spent, decades of effort to find the evidence for this particle called the Higgs boson.
cues.zh: 历经数千人的协同合作、数十亿美元的投入以及数十年的努力，我们终于找到了这种被称为 Higgs 玻色子的粒子证据。

cues.en: So there are two questions that you should be asking about this event. One is, what is the big deal?
cues.zh: 关于这件事，大家应该会问两个问题。第一，这到底有什么了不起的？

cues.en: Of all of the events maybe in humankind, it's hard to think of one that has a greater ratio of excitement generated,
cues.zh: 纵观人类历史，恐怕很难找到另一件事，

cues.en: in the general public divided by people knowing what's going on.
cues.zh: 大众的狂热程度与真正搞懂它的人数之比，会有如此悬殊。

cues.en: It's very difficult to explain why this is a... People get it. You know, they they appreciate. They see the physicists walking around buzzing with excitement but it... They don't actually understand
cues.zh: 很难解释为什么这……大家都知道这很重要，也很佩服，看着物理学家们兴奋得手舞足蹈，但其实……大家根本不明白

cues.en: what the excitement is about.
cues.zh: 他们到底在兴奋什么。

cues.en: Maybe you don't until
cues.zh: 也许在今晚之前，你也不太明白，

cues.en: tonight.
cues.zh: 直到今晚。

cues.en: And the next question of course is what's next? You know, that's good. You've you've done something you've been trying to do for decades. So we're all about, you know, what is happening in the next thirty minutes, or two minutes in the Twitter age. So tell me what we're going to do next. And that's what I want to, talk about a little bit today.
cues.zh: 第二个问题自然是：接下来呢？这很好，你们完成了努力数十年的成果。但在当今这个 Twitter 时代，大家关心的都是接下来的三十分钟、甚至两分钟内会发生什么。所以告诉我，接下来要干什么？这正是今天我想稍微聊聊的。

cues.en: So the story that we're tracing goes back to this guy, Democritus.
cues.zh: 我们追溯的这个故事，要回到这个人身上——Democritus。

cues.en: Democritus,
cues.zh: Democritus，

cues.en: an ancient Greek, he lived two thousand five hundred years ago and he's arguably the first theoretical particle physicist.
cues.zh: 一位古希腊人，生活在两千五百年前，可以说是第一位理论粒子物理学家。

cues.en: He was not an experimental particle physicist. They didn't have those back in ancient Greece. But Democritus and his friends
cues.zh: 他可不是实验粒子物理学家，古希腊那时候可没有这类人。但 Democritus 和他的朋友们，

cues.en: Epicurus,
cues.zh: Epicurus，

cues.en: Lucretius later in ancient Rome, these were the early classical atomists.
cues.zh: 以及后来古罗马的 Lucretius，正是早期的古典原子论者。

cues.en: These were the people who were saying that we look around us, we see this incredible variety of stuff. There are living beings, there is the air, the water, the earth, there is materials around us. And these guys said, you know what? They're not all fundamentally different kinds of things.
cues.zh: 就是这些人，他们说：看看周围，我们看到各种各样不可思议的东西。有生命体，有空气、水、土地，还有我们周围的物质。然后这些人说，你知道吗？它们并不是根本不同类型的东西。

cues.en: They're the same fundamental ingredients arranged in different ways. It's the atoms of different materials, the fundamental particles
cues.zh: 它们是同一些基本成分，以不同方式排列。就是不同物质的原子，也就是基本粒子

cues.en: that put... Get put together in different ways, to make all the wonderful variety we see around us. Now the word atoms which is what they used was sadly stolen by the chemists in the nineteenth century
cues.zh: 它们以不同方式组合在一起，造就了我们周围看到的全部奇妙多样性。而他们当时用的 atoms 这个词，很遗憾在19世纪被化学家抢走了

cues.en: to denote the chemical elements. But what they really were talking about were what we would call elementary particles. The particles of which there's no smaller little pieces.
cues.zh: 用来指化学元素。但他们真正谈论的，是我们所说的基本粒子——也就是没有更小组成部分的粒子。

cues.en: This is not a photograph of Democritus.
cues.zh: 这不是 Democritus 的照片。

cues.en: There are no photographs or even sketches of what Democritus looks like. But in addition to being a famous atomist, he also had a great nickname.
cues.zh: 没有 Democritus 的照片，甚至连画像都没有。不过除了是著名的原子论者，他还有一个很棒的绰号。

cues.en: Democritus was known as the laughing philosopher.
cues.zh: Democritus 被称为“爱笑的哲学家”。

cues.en: So when the Renaissance came along and it became possible to earn a living painting things
cues.zh: 所以文艺复兴到来后，靠画画谋生成为可能

cues.en: and classical subjects were very popular, people would paint self portraits
cues.zh: 而古典题材又非常流行，人们会画自画像

cues.en: and call them Democritus
cues.zh: 并把它叫作 Democritus

cues.en: because they wanted to paint a self portrait themselves laughing.
cues.zh: 因为他们想画一幅自己正在笑的自画像。

cues.en: So this is Rembrandt, the young Rembrandt, he labeled it Democritus,
cues.zh: 所以这是 Rembrandt，年轻的 Rembrandt，他把画标为 Democritus，

cues.en: doubles the price at the auction, for your painting.
cues.zh: 在拍卖会上，这能让你的画价格翻倍。

cues.en: Now twenty five hundred years later, where do we find ourselves?
cues.zh: 两千五百年后的今天，我们又走到了哪里？

cues.en: The the particle physics as we currently understand it is is truly something that really got going in the twentieth century. There were, you know, little things going on in the nineteenth century as well. But by the nineteen thirties,
cues.zh: 我们如今所理解的粒子物理学，其实真正起步于二十世纪。虽然在十九世纪，你知道，也有一些零星的进展。但到了二十世纪三十年代，

cues.en: we had put together a pretty good picture
cues.zh: 我们已经拼凑出了一幅相当清晰的图景，

cues.en: of what matter and and forces are.
cues.zh: 弄清了物质与力究竟是什么。

cues.en: You could have forgiven a 1935
cues.zh: 如果1935年

cues.en: era physicist from thinking that, you know, we were pretty close to getting it all right. We had this idea that,
cues.zh: 那个时代的物理学家认为，我们已经快要把一切都搞清楚了，你完全可以理解。当时我们的认识是，

cues.en: there were atoms
cues.zh: 物质由原子构成，

cues.en: and people like Rutherford and Bohr had put together pictures of how the atoms worked. The atom was not, there were old ideas of plum pudding and so forth but the new idea is that there is a small dense nucleus at the center of the atom and there are electrons, lighter particles electrically charged orbiting around the nucleus.
cues.zh: 像 Rutherford 和 Bohr 这样的人已经勾勒出了原子的运作图景。原子并不是——之前有枣糕模型等旧说法，但新观念是，原子中心有一个致密微小的原子核，外面有带电的较轻粒子，也就是电子，正绕着原子核运转。

cues.en: And since then people learned that the nucleus was a combination of positively charged particles called protons,
cues.zh: 从那时起，人们认识到原子核是由带正电的质子，

cues.en: neutral particles called neutrons.
cues.zh: 和不带电的中子组合而成的。

cues.en: What kind of chemical element you have just depends on how many protons you have. So you have three particles protons,
cues.zh: 具体属于哪种化学元素，只取决于你有多少个质子。所以这就有了三种粒子：质子、

cues.en: neutrons, electrons
cues.zh: 中子、电子，

cues.en: and there were three forces
cues.zh: 此外还有三种

cues.en: that were pushing them around. There's the electromagnetic
cues.zh: 推动它们相互作用的力。首先是电磁

cues.en: force. Back in the nineteenth century, we unified
cues.zh: 力。早在十九世纪，我们就统一了

cues.en: electric
cues.zh: 电学——

cues.en: electricity and magnetism.
cues.zh: 电与磁。

cues.en: The electromagnetic force takes the negatively charged electron and pulls it toward the positively charged proton.
cues.zh: 电磁力让带负电的电子被带正电的质子吸引。

cues.en: There is some nuclear force. No one knew anything about that in 1935 but they knew that something was making the protons and neutrons stick together.
cues.zh: 还存在某种核力。1935年没人了解它，但人们知道有某种东西把质子和中子粘在一起。

cues.en: So there's some nuclear force that holds them together and then there's gravity. Gravity pulls everything to everything else. It's absolutely universal. It's shameless gravity. It does the same thing to everybody.
cues.zh: 所以有某种核力把它们聚在一起，然后还有引力。引力把一切拉向一切。它绝对普遍，简直一视同仁，对谁都一样。

cues.en: And the remarkable thing is that in the course of scientific progress we learn more things. Sometimes that learning causes us to throw out
cues.zh: 了不起的是，在科学进步的过程中我们会学到更多。有时这种学习会让我们抛弃

cues.en: previous knowledge. Sometimes we just absorb and expand on it. This picture that we put together in 1935
cues.zh: 已有知识。有时我们只是吸收并扩展它。我们1935年拼出的这幅图景

cues.en: remains true
cues.zh: 仍然成立

cues.en: to this day and it will remain true forever.
cues.zh: 直到今天，而且将永远成立。

cues.en: It will always be true that people like you and me are made of atoms that are made of electrons, protons and neutrons. We've added to the picture so such so that by the nineteen eighties,
cues.zh: 像你我这样的人由原子构成，原子由电子、质子和中子构成，这一点将永远成立。我们不断扩充这幅图景，以至于到20世纪80年代，

cues.en: here is the kind of picture we had. So we knew that there are still protons and neutrons but we know they're not elementary particles.
cues.zh: 我们当时有的图景是这样的。我们知道仍然存在质子和中子，但也知道它们不是基本粒子。

cues.en: Protons and neutrons, the nucleons, the stuff that make up the nucleus are actually made of smaller particles called quarks.
cues.zh: 质子、中子，也就是核子，构成原子核的东西，实际上由更小的粒子——夸克组成。

cues.en: We had the up quark, the down quark
cues.zh: 我们有上夸克、下夸克

cues.en: and there's two ups and a down in a proton, two downs and an up in a neutron. So it's a very simple picture of how to put together
cues.zh: 质子中有两个上夸克和一个下夸克，中子中有两个下夸克和一个上夸克。所以，要组合成……其实是一幅很简单的图景

cues.en: protons and neutrons.
cues.zh: 质子和中子。

cues.en: Then we needed one more particle because the nuclear force got split in two. And because particle physicists are brilliant at naming things,
cues.zh: 然后我们需要再多一种粒子，因为核力被分成了两种。而且因为粒子物理学家特别擅长命名，

cues.en: they called it the strong nuclear force and the weak nuclear force.
cues.zh: 他们把它叫作强核力和弱核力。

cues.en: That... There's a little footnote saying that was sarcastic when I said the particle physicists are brilliant at naming things.
cues.zh: 那个……有个小脚注说，我说粒子物理学家特别擅长命名时是在讽刺。

cues.en: The, strong nuclear force is what holds the quark together, the quarks inside the nucleons. And then there's like extra leakage of the strong force is what actually holds the neutrons and protons themselves together. But there's something else that goes on. Inside the sun, for example, when two protons smack together,
cues.zh: 强核力把夸克束缚在一起，也就是核子内部的夸克。然后强核力还有额外的泄漏，实际上把中子和质子本身束缚在一起。但还有别的事情发生。比如在太阳内部，当两个质子撞在一起，

cues.en: they fuse.
cues.zh: 它们会聚变。

cues.en: But what that means is that one of those protons turns into a neutron.
cues.zh: 但这意味着其中一个质子变成了中子。

cues.en: Where does the extra electric charge go? It spits out an electron and... Or an anti electron and then another particle called the neutrino.
cues.zh: 多出来的电荷去哪了？它吐出一个电子……或者说一个反电子，还有一个叫中微子的粒子。

cues.en: This is not run by the strong nuclear force. It's a whole new force called the weak nuclear force. It needs the neutrino to make it work. But otherwise, the picture is the same. So instead of three particles and three forces,
cues.zh: 这不是由强核力驱动的。而是一种全新的力，叫弱核力。它需要中微子才能起作用。除此之外，图景是一样的。所以不是三种粒子和三种力，

cues.en: we have four particles and four forces.
cues.zh: 而是四种粒子和四种力。

cues.en: Over fifty years of effort and we made one more particle and one more force.
cues.zh: 五十多年的努力，我们只多发现了一种粒子和一种力。

cues.en: But sadly, it's a little more complicated than that. The the other rule to thinking about if you want to guess about the future of Physics,
cues.zh: 但遗憾的是，情况还要更复杂一点。思考物理学未来的另一条规则是，

cues.en: just guess what is it that will make the lives of Physics graduate students the most difficult.
cues.zh: 就猜猜什么会让物理学研究生的生活最艰难。

cues.en: So we took this picture, it works very well and then we duplicated it three times. So
cues.zh: 于是我们采用了这幅图景，它非常管用，接着我们把它复制了三份。所以

cues.en: there's not only an up quark, down quark, an electron and neutrino,
cues.zh: 不仅有上夸克、下夸克、电子和中微子，

cues.en: that family of particles or that generation within a family, there's another generation of heavier particles and another generation heavier than that.
cues.zh: 这一族粒子，或者说族内的这一代粒子，还有另一代更重的粒子，以及比它还要更重的一代。

cues.en: The first one of these we found, the electron and its heavier cousin is called the muon.
cues.zh: 我们在这类粒子中找到的第一个——电子那个更重的“表亲”，叫做缪子。

cues.en: And literally, the famous physicist I. Rabi, when the muon was discovered, he said, who ordered that?
cues.zh: 毫不夸张地说，著名物理学家 I. Rabi 在发现缪子时就曾说：“这是谁点的？”

cues.en: The muon does nothing useful to us. It just is a heavier cousin of the electron and there is another heavier one called the tau.
cues.zh: 缪子对我们毫无用处，它只是电子更重的表亲，而且还有一个更重的叫陶子。

cues.en: And the up and the down quarks, have heavier cousins called charm and strange and yet heavier ones called top and bottom.

cues.en: what we can do next now that we've discovered that Higgs boson.

cues.en: So when people talk about the Higgs boson, they're always start... They talk... Talking about mass. Right? You've heard this. You can't avoid this. They start talking about how the Higgs boson is what gives particles mass.
cues.zh: 当人们谈论希格斯玻色子时，总是先……他们谈……谈论质量。对吧？你们肯定听过，根本避不开。他们开口就是希格斯玻色子是如何赋予粒子质量的。

cues.en: And I struggled in... Because, you know, I was writing a book about the Higgs boson. Did I mention I've written a book about the Higgs boson
cues.zh: 我当时也很犯难……因为你们知道，我那时正在写一本关于希格斯玻色子的书。我提过我写了一本关于希格斯玻色子的书吗？

cues.en: right now on your iPhone. You don't need to wait. You could buy that in Amazon right now.
cues.zh: 就在你们的 iPhone 上，不用等，现在就能在 Amazon 上买到。

cues.en: And it's difficult to explain why you need a Higgs field to give mass to particles. So I thought about why the Higgs field was inventive. What were they thinking? And I realized they weren't thinking about giving mass to particles at all.
cues.zh: 要解释为什么需要希格斯场来赋予粒子质量非常困难。所以我去思考希格斯场究竟因何被构想出来。他们当时在想什么？后来我意识到，他们当时根本就没考虑过给粒子赋予质量这件事。

cues.en: They were thinking about how forces
cues.zh: 他们在思考力是如何

cues.en: work in nature.
cues.zh: 在自然中工作。

cues.en: And the way that forces work, remember Newton
cues.zh: 至于力的作用方式，还记得牛顿吧

cues.en: told us about gravity, an inverse square law. The gravitational field fades away as you get further and further away. Why is that? There's a simple geometric
cues.zh: 告诉我们引力遵循平方反比定律。引力场随着你离得越来越远而逐渐减弱。为什么会这样？有一个简单的几何

cues.en: reasoning. It's because the lines of force
cues.zh: 推理逻辑。这是因为力线

cues.en: get diluted as you go further away. It's just like that lantern moving away from you. Its brightness also obeys
cues.zh: 距离越远就越会被减弱。就像那盏离你远去的灯笼一样，它的亮度也同样遵循

cues.en: an inverse square law. It gets dimmer because there are fewer lines of light rays hitting your eyeballs.
cues.zh: 平方反比定律。它变暗，是因为射到你眼球上的光线变少了。

cues.en: Not only does gravity work this way but electromagnetism
cues.zh: 不仅引力如此，电磁力也是这样

cues.en: also works this way.
cues.zh: 也是同样的道理。

cues.en: However, the weak force and the strong force, the nuclear forces very dramatically do not work this way.
cues.zh: 然而，弱力和强力，也就是核力，却非常明显地不是这样运作的。

cues.en: They do not stretch over the long distances that gravity and electromagnetism do. They only stretch over very short distances.
cues.zh: 它们的作用距离不像引力和电磁力那么远。它们只在极短的距离内起作用。

cues.en: The problem that was bugging the people in the nineteen sixties when they invented the Higgs field is why
cues.zh: 20世纪60年代人们提出希格斯场时，困扰他们的问题是：为什么

cues.en: are the nuclear forces so short range?
cues.zh: 核力为什么这么短程？

cues.en: This is not an accident. This is just math.
cues.zh: 这不是偶然。这只是数学。

cues.en: How is the math avoided?
cues.zh: 数学是怎么被绕开的？

cues.en: Remember again,
cues.zh: 再强调一次，

cues.en: nature will always choose the ways that makes graduate students in Physics the most, annoyed.
cues.zh: 大自然总是会选择让物理系研究生最抓狂的方式。

cues.en: So it turns out that the answer, why is the force short range is utterly different for the strong nuclear force and the weak nuclear force.
cues.zh: 问题的答案是，强核力和弱核力的作用范围之所以很短，原因完全不同。

cues.en: For the strong nuclear force, there's something called confinement.
cues.zh: 对于强核力，有一种现象叫禁闭。

cues.en: The lines of force don't just stretch out to infinity,
cues.zh: 力线不会只是无限延伸，

cues.en: they interact with each other.
cues.zh: 它们会彼此相互作用。

cues.en: Strong nuclear force, fittingly, is strong.
cues.zh: 顾名思义，强核力很强。

cues.en: So what happens is that all the lines of force get bundled together and it's like they're trapped. It's like someone put a shutter around that lantern and if your head is inside the shutter, it looks very bright. And if it's outside, you don't see the lantern at all. If your head was inside a proton, the strong force would seem very strong.
cues.zh: 所以，所有力线都会被束缚在一起，就好像被困住了一样。就像有人在那盏灯笼周围装上了遮板：如果你的头在遮板里面，它看起来就非常明亮；而如果你的头在外面，你根本看不到灯笼。如果你的头在质子里面，强核力看起来就会非常强。

cues.en: If it's outside, you don't notice a strong force at all. That's confinement. Various Nobel Prizes were given away for that.
cues.zh: 如果你在外面，根本感觉不到强核力。这就是禁闭。为此还颁发过好几次诺贝尔奖。

cues.en: The weak nuclear force is not confined.
cues.zh: 弱核力并没有被禁闭。

cues.en: It is absorbed.
cues.zh: 它会被吸收。

cues.en: What if that lantern walking away from you at night was on a foggy night?
cues.zh: 如果那盏在夜里离你而去的灯笼，所在的夜晚还有雾呢？

cues.en: Then as soon as it gets a little distance away, you suddenly don't see it at all. The light coming from the lantern is absorbed by the fog.
cues.zh: 那么它一拉开一点距离，你突然就完全看不见它了。灯笼发出的光被雾吸收了。

cues.en: The brilliant idea from the early nineteen sixties was the following.
cues.zh: 20世纪60年代初，有人提出了一个绝妙的想法。

cues.en: Maybe there's a field that we haven't thought of yet that fills all of space
cues.zh: 也许存在一种我们还没想到的场，它充满整个空间，

cues.en: and absorbs the lines of force from the weak nuclear force.
cues.zh: 并吸收弱核力的力线。

cues.en: And that's why it's short range. The lines of force just don't get very far until they are absorbed by this foggy field
cues.zh: 这就是它作用距离很短的原因。力线还没传播多远，就会被这个雾一样的场吸收，

cues.en: that pervades all of space.
cues.zh: 而这个场遍布整个空间。

cues.en: So just to say the same thing in different, words,
cues.zh: 换句话说，

cues.en: this thing that we now call the Higgs field, it was invented by like seven or eight different people but Higgs has the coolest sounding last name so his name gets attached to it.
cues.zh: 这个如今被称为希格斯场的东西，是七八位不同的人分别提出的，只是 Higgs 这个姓听起来最酷，所以最后就用他的名字来命名了。

cues.en: All of the other fields that we know about in nature,
cues.zh: 我们在自然界中已知的所有其他场，

cues.en: if you plot the value of the field, remember that's what a field is. It's something that takes on a value everywhere.
cues.zh: 如果你画出场的值，记住场就是这个意思。它在每一点都有一个值。

cues.en: Well, it it hovers around zero in empty space. If there's a particle there, it will be vibrating but most of the time the fields are just sitting there at zero whether it's a electromagnetic field, gluon field, the quarks or whatever.
cues.zh: 在真空中它围绕零波动。如果有粒子在那里，它就会振动，但大多数时候场就待在零处，无论是电磁场、胶子场、夸克场还是别的什么。

cues.en: The Higgs field is way up here.
cues.zh: 希格斯场却高高在上。

cues.en: Its value in empty space
cues.zh: 它在真空中的值

cues.en: is not zero. So you see the drama of what is being suggested.
cues.zh: 不是零。所以你能看出这其中的戏剧性了。

cues.en: These guys were saying, no no no. It's not the weak interactions that are puzzling. It's that you don't understand empty space.
cues.zh: 这些人说，不不不。令人困惑的不是弱相互作用。而是你不理解真空。

cues.en: It has a field in it that has tangible effects we can go out and measure. For example, if you poke at it, if you poke this field, you make a particle. We'll call it the Higgs boson.
cues.zh: 真空里有一个场，它有实实在在的效应，我们可以去测量。比如，如果你去戳它，戳这个场，你就会造出一个粒子。我们称之为希格斯玻色子。

cues.en: And that's what we've been looking for for the forty some years since the idea was put forward.
cues.zh: 这正是自这个想法提出四十多年来我们一直在寻找的东西。

cues.en: It was as a bonus. It was in 1967 that Steven Weinberg pointed out that if you take this idea that they were actually thinking mostly of the strong nuclear force. But if you apply it to the weak nuclear force, Weinberg said, you get a bonus which is you can explain how particles get mass. This is a little puzzle that most people weren't even really taking very seriously but in the theories of the day, you couldn't explain
cues.zh: 这算是额外收获。1967年Steven Weinberg指出，如果你采用这个想法——他们当时主要想的是强核力。但如果你把它应用到弱核力上，Weinberg说，你会得到一个额外收获，那就是你能解释粒子如何获得质量。这是个小谜题，大多数人甚至没太当回事，但在当时的理论中，你无法解释

cues.en: why particles like the electrons and the quarks had mass at all. That's because... I'm not gonna tell you why that's because. It's a whole thing and you don't wanna go there. But given
cues.zh: 为什么像电子和夸克这样的粒子会有质量。这是因为……我不会告诉你这是因为什么。说来话长，你不会想深究的。但考虑到

cues.en: the fact that the world looks different in a mirror,
cues.zh: 世界在镜子里看起来不一样，

cues.en: the fact that parity,
cues.zh: 考虑到宇称，

cues.en: the symmetry that you'd like to see in the world between,
cues.zh: 你希望在世界中看到的对称性，

cues.en: things that we see in front of us and things that they would observe, be observed in a mirror world, in particular the weak interactions
cues.zh: 即我们眼前看到的东西和在镜中世界会观察到的东西之间的对称性，特别是弱相互作用

cues.en: treat reality one way and
cues.zh: 以一种方式对待现实，而

cues.en: mirror reality a different way is a simple argument that says that that means that every single particle that a weak interaction interacts with moves at the speed of light, has to have zero mass. Einstein told us a long time ago if a particle is massless,
cues.zh: 镜中现实则以另一种方式对待，这是一个简单的论证，说明这意味着弱相互作用所作用的每一个粒子都以光速运动，必须质量为零。Einstein很久以前就告诉我们，如果一个粒子没有质量，

cues.en: it zips along at the speed of light. You can never slow it down.
cues.zh: 它就以光速飞驰。你永远无法让它慢下来。

cues.en: That would be bad
cues.zh: 那就糟了

cues.en: if that were true.
cues.zh: 如果真是这样的话。

cues.en: If the electron were massless,
cues.zh: 如果电子没有质量，

cues.en: remember electrons are important. They form atoms. Right? They're the things that go around the nucleus.
cues.zh: 记住电子很重要。它们构成原子。对吧？它们就是绕着原子核转的东西。

cues.en: So if you want to have two atoms come together to make chemistry, it's the electrons that are doing the work.
cues.zh: 所以如果你想让两个原子凑到一起产生化学作用，干活的就是电子。

cues.en: If the electron were massless, it would not ever stick to a nucleus.
cues.zh: 如果电子没有质量，它就永远粘不住原子核。

cues.en: If the electron were massless, there would be no such thing as atoms.
cues.zh: 如果电子没有质量，就不会有原子这种东西。

cues.en: There would be no such thing as molecules or chemistry or life.
cues.zh: 也不会有分子、化学或者生命。

cues.en: The world with massless electrons would be very very boring place indeed. There would be no Fermi lab, no public lectures, nothing like that.
cues.zh: 电子没有质量的世界会是一个非常非常无聊的地方。不会有费米实验室，不会有公开讲座，什么都没有。

cues.en: So Weinberg says if you fill space with this Higgs field,
cues.zh: 所以温伯格说，如果你用这个希格斯场填满空间，

cues.en: I can cook up a model where the electron interacts.
cues.zh: 我就能构造一个电子在其中相互作用的模型。

cues.en: The electron feels the influence of the Higgs field all around it
cues.zh: 电子感受到周围希格斯场的影响

cues.en: and that gives it some heft.
cues.zh: 这就给了它一些分量。

cues.en: It makes it harder to push the electron and get it moving. It gives it some mass.
cues.zh: 这让推动电子、让它动起来变得更难。这就给了它一些质量。

cues.en: It turns out to be spectacularly confirmed. This is a model that made many many predictions that all come true,
cues.zh: 结果这个模型被惊人地证实了。这个模型做出了很多很多预测，全都应验了，

cues.en: to very high precision.
cues.zh: 精度非常高。

cues.en: So the Higgs boson is what makes life itself
cues.zh: 所以希格斯玻色子是让生命本身

cues.en: possible. That is why discovering it was a big deal.
cues.zh: 成为可能的东西。这就是为什么发现它是一件大事。

cues.en: Now
cues.zh: 现在

cues.en: if you want to know about new physics we haven't yet discovered including, let's say I was giving this talk, a year ago, we haven't discovered the Higgs boson yet. How do you look for new physics? How do you look for physics you don't yet know?
cues.zh: 如果你想知道我们还没发现的新物理，比如说，假如这是一年前的演讲，我们还没发现希格斯玻色子。你怎么寻找新物理？你怎么寻找你还不知道的物理？

cues.en: It turns out that quantum field theory
cues.zh: 事实证明，量子场论

cues.en: tells you how to look for things you haven't found yet. This is like an amazingly wonderful fact because in classical mechanics, you can just imagine all sorts of different ways that weird phenomena could hide from you. But this idea that the world is made of fields and the fields vibrate and they all talk to each other,
cues.zh: 会告诉你如何寻找尚未发现的事物。这真是个妙不可言的事实，因为在经典力学中，各种离奇现象有无数种方式隐匿起来。但“世界由场构成，场在振动且彼此相互作用”这种观念，

cues.en: that tells you how to look for new fields. You shake the fields that you know hard enough, they will start the other fields vibrating.
cues.zh: 告诉你该如何寻找新的场。只要足够剧烈地扰动已知的场，它们就会带动其他场振动起来。

cues.en: And you can basically put all the new kinds of interactions on a little plot. You have a new particle, a new field. Tell me two things. Tell me number one how massive it is.
cues.zh: 你基本上可以把所有新型相互作用都画在一张简图上。有了新粒子、新场，只要告诉我两件事：第一，它的质量有多大。

cues.en: And mass in physics corresponds to short distances because
cues.zh: 在物理学中，质量对应着短距离，因为

cues.en: a mass is a vibration and the wavelength being short means the energy is high which means there's high mass.
cues.zh: 质量本身就是一种振动，波长短意味着能量高，也就意味着质量大。

cues.en: So there's heavy particles that are corresponding to short ranges and high energies. There are light particles that correspond to long ranges or low energies. That's one thing you have to tell me. And then tell me how that particle interacts with other particles.
cues.zh: 所以，重粒子对应短距离和高能量；轻粒子对应长距离或低能量。这是你要告诉我的第一点。然后再告诉我，该粒子如何与其他粒子发生相互作用。

cues.en: Is it only a little bit or is it very strongly?
cues.zh: 是只有极其微弱的作用，还是非常强烈？

cues.en: You will not be surprised to learn that the things we can access,
cues.zh: 你肯定不会感到意外：我们能够触及的事物，

cues.en: the known knowns, the things we've already discovered are the ones that stretch over large distances and interact strongly.
cues.zh: 即那些“已知的已知”、那些我们早已发现的事物，往往跨越很大距离并且相互作用极强。

cues.en: The things we haven't found yet are those that are either too heavy,
cues.zh: 我们尚未发现的东西，要么是质量太大、

cues.en: we haven't had the energy to make them or too weakly interacting.
cues.zh: 我们还没有足够的能量制造它们，要么是相互作用太弱。

cues.en: Those are the known unknowns in David Rumsfeld's famous formulation.
cues.zh: 用 David Rumsfeld 的名言来说，这些是“已知的未知”。

cues.en: The
cues.zh: 而

cues.en: unknown unknowns would just be the idea that quantum field theory is not right which is of course always possible. There's just no evidence for it right now.
cues.zh: “未知的未知”则是量子场论可能根本不对——这当然随时都有可能，只是目前还没有任何证据。

cues.en: So two different strategies
cues.zh: 所以寻找新物理现象

cues.en: for looking for new physical phenomena. Go to higher energies,
cues.zh: 有两种不同的策略。走向更高的能级，

cues.en: build a giant particle accelerator, smash things together as fast as you can or look for very very weak interactions. Look for very subtle tiny high precision effects.
cues.zh: 建造巨大的粒子加速器，让粒子以尽可能高的速度对撞；或者去寻找极其微弱的相互作用，寻找非常微妙、微小的超高精度效应。

cues.en: And we are doing both.
cues.zh: 而这两点我们都在做。

cues.en: The Tevatron right next door here at Fermilab and the Large Hadron Collider which is its spiritual successor
cues.zh: 就在隔壁 Fermilab 的 Tevatron，以及作为其精神续作的 Large Hadron Collider，

cues.en: were the high energy
cues.zh: 走的都是高能

cues.en: route. This was the energy is the energy frontier. You just go to as high an energy as you can. You try to make new stuff.
cues.zh: 路线。这就是能量前沿。尽可能冲向更高的能量，尝试制造出新的东西。

cues.en: Here is Fermilab. The Tevatron was recently decommissioned
cues.zh: 这里就是 Fermilab。Tevatron 不久前退役了，

cues.en: like, like the old battleship that it was. The Large Hadron Collider is in outside
cues.zh: 就像一艘功成身退的老战列舰。Large Hadron Collider 则位于

cues.en: Geneva at CERN. It's where the Higgs boson was discovered. The ATLAS and CMS experiments
cues.zh: 日内瓦郊外的 CERN。Higgs boson 就是在那里被发现的。ATLAS 和 CMS 实验

cues.en: are there.
cues.zh: 也都在那儿。

cues.en: You can't actually see
cues.zh: 在地面上你其实根本看不到

cues.en: the Large Hadron Collider from the ground because it's 300 feet underground. You could be standing on top of it and not know. Fermilab, at least you can see, which I think any honest accelerator should be visible from an airplane.
cues.zh: Large Hadron Collider，因为它深埋在地下 300 英尺。你就算站在它头顶上也浑然不知。但至少 Fermilab 是看得到的——我觉得任何像样的加速器，从飞机上都应该能一眼看到。

cues.en: So what happens? What do these things do? They
cues.zh: 那会发生什么呢？这些东西是做什么的？它们

cues.en: take protons.
cues.zh: 拿质子。

cues.en: Fermilab took protons and antiprotons.
cues.zh: 费米实验室拿质子和反质子。

cues.en: CERN just takes protons and you smash them together and you watch what comes out. And here's what comes out. Well, what comes out is a lot. The problem is a proton is a mess. You smash it together and, you know, lots of things come out. So there's so many things coming out and they're governed by the rules of quantum mechanics
cues.zh: CERN只拿质子，把它们撞在一起，然后观察出来什么。结果出来的是什么呢？出来的东西很多。问题在于质子是一团乱麻。你把它撞在一起，你知道，很多东西会出来。所以有太多东西出来，而且它们受量子力学规律支配

cues.en: that when it will be... At the LHC,
cues.zh: 以至于当它会是……在LHC，

cues.en: when two particles, two protons come together and collide and have an event,
cues.zh: 当两个粒子、两个质子相遇碰撞并产生一个事件时，

cues.en: you throw away the data about 999,999
cues.zh: 你会丢弃大约999,999

cues.en: times out of a million.
cues.zh: 百万分之九十九万九千九百九十九的数据。

cues.en: Usually what happens in an event is just stuff we knew was going to happen. It's that one in a million thing that looks interesting and then we keep it. And so a lot of the effort in particle physics is making sure we keep the right data.
cues.zh: 通常一个事件里发生的只是我们早就知道会发生的东西。正是那百万分之一看起来有趣的东西，我们才保留下来。所以粒子物理学的大量工作就是确保我们保留正确的数据。

cues.en: So you know, you there's an analogy that is often used here that doing particle physics is like smashing two watches together and trying to figure out how watches work by watching all the pieces fall apart. Right?
cues.zh: 所以你知道，这里常用一个类比：做粒子物理学就像把两块手表砸在一起，然后通过观察所有碎片散落来弄清楚手表是如何运作的。对吧？

cues.en: This analogy is terrible
cues.zh: 这个类比很糟糕

cues.en: for many reasons.
cues.zh: 原因很多。

cues.en: The primary one is that what's coming out
cues.zh: 主要的一点是，当你把粒子撞在一起时，出来的东西

cues.en: when you smash particles together is not what was inside the original particles. Remember what's really going on are vibrating fields
cues.zh: 并不是原始粒子内部的东西。记住，真正发生的是振动的场

cues.en: vibrating to beat the band at incredibly high energies and their mutual vibrations brings new vibrations
cues.zh: 以极高的能量剧烈振动，它们相互的振动带来新的振动

cues.en: into existence in other fields.
cues.zh: 在其他场中产生。

cues.en: So when the Higgs boson pops out of a proton proton collision, it's not because there was a Higgs boson hiding
cues.zh: 当希格斯玻色子从质子-质子碰撞中冒出来时，并不是因为质子中藏着希格斯玻色子

cues.en: in the protons, it's because you made it. It's like you smashed two Timex watches together and a Rolex pops out.
cues.zh: 而是因为你把它造出来了。就像你把两块天美时手表砸在一起，结果蹦出了一块劳力士。

cues.en: And this is this... You might think this is very difficult to do making Rolexes that way. There has to be a cheaper way.
cues.zh: 这……你可能会觉得用这种方式造劳力士太难了。总得有更便宜的办法吧。

cues.en: For the case of precision watches, there is. For the case of particle physics, this is how we need to do it.
cues.zh: 对于精密手表来说，确实有。但对于粒子物理来说，这就是我们不得不采用的方式。

cues.en: The puzzle here, the problem, the issue, the fact of life
cues.zh: 这里的谜题、问题、麻烦、现实情况

cues.en: is that there is no unique signature that says, look, we found the Higgs boson.
cues.zh: 就是：没有任何独一无二的信号能说"看，我们找到了希格斯玻色子"。

cues.en: The Higgs boson never shows up in your detector.
cues.zh: 希格斯玻色子从不会直接出现在你的探测器里。

cues.en: It decays. It has a very short lifetime. The lifetime of a Higgs boson is about one zeptosecond
cues.zh: 它会衰变。它的寿命极短。希格斯玻色子的寿命大约是一仄秒

cues.en: which is very short period of time.
cues.zh: 这是极其短暂的一瞬间。

cues.en: Far too short to be noticeable in our detectors.
cues.zh: 短到在我们的探测器中根本察觉不到。

cues.en: So what we do is we ask, well, what does it decay into?
cues.zh: 所以我们能做的是去问：它衰变成什么？

cues.en: And then theorists come back and say, well, a whole mess of stuff. It is a whole pie chart of possibilities for what the Higgs could decay into.
cues.zh: 然后理论家回来说：一大堆东西。希格斯玻色子可能衰变成什么是整整一张饼图的可能性。

cues.en: And every one of these possibilities can be produced without making a Higgs boson.
cues.zh: 而其中每一种可能性，都可以在不产生希格斯玻色子的情况下发生。

cues.en: So sometimes people say that looking for the Higgs is like looking for a needle in a haystack. But again, that's a wildly optimistic
cues.zh: 所以有时人们说，寻找希格斯玻色子就像大海捞针。但再说一次，这已经是极其乐观的

cues.en: analogy.
cues.zh: 比喻了。

cues.en: When you find the needle in the haystack, you know.
cues.zh: 当你在草堆里找到针时，你是知道的。

cues.en: Looking for the Higgs boson of the LHC is like looking for hay
cues.zh: 而在LHC寻找希格斯玻色子，就像在草堆里找草

cues.en: in a haystack.
cues.zh: 一样。

cues.en: It's like saying that you stack every single stalk of hay in your stack and you're looking for a slightly statistically
cues.zh: 这就像说，你把每一根干草都堆进草堆，然后寻找一个在统计上略微

cues.en: significant
cues.zh: 显著的

cues.en: excess at a certain length of haystalk.
cues.zh: 在特定长度草茎上的超出量。

cues.en: And this is why we have charming and highly paid particle physicists going through, the data and what they give us is this.
cues.zh: 这就是为什么我们有迷人又高薪的粒子物理学家去翻数据，而他们给我们的就是这个。

cues.en: These are the plots that were presented,
cues.zh: 这些就是展示过的图，

cues.en: back in July at CERN. When I wrote my book, I don't know if I mentioned the book, but when I wrote my book,
cues.zh: 早在7月于CERN。我写书时，不确定我提没提过这本书，但我写书时，

cues.en: these were the two plots that my publisher said, you know, I think that's one step too far. We can't include these plots. They look they look a little science y. I mean there's numbers, there's error bars.
cues.zh: 这两张图就是我的出版商说，我觉得这有点太过了。我们不能收录这些图。它们看起来有点太像科学图表了。我是说，有数字，有误差棒。

cues.en: They might be scary.
cues.zh: 它们可能会吓人。

cues.en: And I said in a very short email, said we paid $9,000,000,000
cues.zh: 我在一封很短的邮件里说，我们花了90亿美元

cues.en: for these plots. They should go in the book.
cues.zh: 就为了这些图。它们应该放进书里。

cues.en: He said okay.
cues.zh: 他说好。

cues.en: So what are you looking at? What you're looking at, this is the energy that comes out when two photons
cues.zh: 所以你在看什么？你看到的是两个光子产生时释放的能量

cues.en: are produced. So you make these these terribly complicated
cues.zh: 产生的。所以你把这些极其复杂的

cues.en: protons smashing together.
cues.zh: 质子撞在一起。

cues.en: Two very high energy photons come out and a bunch of lower energy stuff. Here's the energy in those photons. Here's how many times
cues.zh: 两个非常高能的光子出来，还有一堆低能的东西。这些光子的能量在这里。出现多少次

cues.en: you get events with that kind of energy. The smooth downward sloping curve is what you would predict if there were no Higgs bosons lurking around.
cues.zh: 你得到那种能量的事件。平滑下降的曲线就是如果没有希格斯玻色子潜伏时的预测。

cues.en: The tiny little bump,
cues.zh: 那个小小的凸起，

cues.en: that is because that at this energy,
cues.zh: 是因为在这个能量下，

cues.en: you first made a Higgs boson and then the Higgs boson decayed into two photons.
cues.zh: 你先产生了一个希格斯玻色子，然后希格斯玻色子衰变成两个光子。

cues.en: So it's not a different type of thing in any fundamental sense. It's just a slightly
cues.zh: 所以从根本上说，它并不是另一种不同的东西。只是稍微

cues.en: higher amount
cues.zh: 更高数量

cues.en: of photons are produced with this energy because you created a new way to make them by first making a Higgs boson then letting that decay. Now to the skeptical eye,
cues.zh: 的光子以这种能量产生，因为你创造了一种新的方式：先制造希格斯玻色子，然后让它衰变。现在，对于持怀疑眼光的人来说，

cues.en: these bumps aren't very big.
cues.zh: 这些隆起并不大。

cues.en: In fact, if they hadn't drawn the red line there, you might not have noticed that there was a bump there.
cues.zh: 事实上，如果他们没在那里画那条红线，你可能根本不会注意到那里有个隆起。

cues.en: But
cues.zh: 但

cues.en: number one, trust me, they do the math. This is a one in a million chance that you would get a bump that big if it were not real. And number two, there are two plots
cues.zh: 第一，相信我，他们做了数学计算。如果它不是真的，你得到那么大隆起的概率是百万分之一。第二，有两张图

cues.en: for two very
cues.zh: 对应两组非常

cues.en: competitive sets of experimenters
cues.zh: 有竞争力的实验团队

cues.en: and they find exactly the same bump in exactly the same place. There's no question that there is a new particle here and that we now know it is something that we were looking for called the Higgs boson.
cues.zh: 他们在完全相同的位置发现了完全相同的隆起。毫无疑问，这里有一种新粒子，而且我们现在知道它就是我们一直在寻找的希格斯玻色子。

cues.en: So that leaves us in a bittersweet
cues.zh: 所以这让我们处于一个苦乐参半的

cues.en: reality.
cues.zh: 现实中。

cues.en: The good news is that we understand
cues.zh: 好消息是，我们理解了

cues.en: all of the laws of physics underlying
cues.zh: 支撑你现在周围所见一切的

cues.en: everything that you see around you right now.
cues.zh: 所有物理定律。

cues.en: That is to say as you go through your life,
cues.zh: 也就是说，在你的一生中，

cues.en: the things that if unless you're a working particle physicist, as you go through your life just using your eyes,
cues.zh: 除非你是职业粒子物理学家，否则在你的一生中，你只是用眼睛、

cues.en: listening with your ears, touching things with your fingers, everything you experience
cues.zh: 用耳朵听、用手指触摸东西，你所经历的一切

cues.en: is explained
cues.zh: 都可以解释

cues.en: by the physics we now understand
cues.zh: 由我们现在理解的物理学

cues.en: By these atoms and the other elementary particles and I added to the background here the Higgs boson field.
cues.zh: 由这些原子和其他基本粒子，我在这里的背景中还加入了希格斯玻色子场。

cues.en: We understand gravity.
cues.zh: 我们理解引力。

cues.en: All the underlying stuff that makes up you, me, the earth, the sun, the moon, the stars, the podium, your cat.
cues.zh: 构成你、我、地球、太阳、月亮、星星、讲台以及你的猫的所有底层物质。

cues.en: This is all physics we now understand.
cues.zh: 这些都是我们现在已经理解的物理。

cues.en: And I know what you're thinking. You're thinking, well, I'm not going to believe a grandiose claim like that unless you show me the equations. I know that
cues.zh: 我知道你在想什么。你在想：除非你给我看方程，否则我不会相信这么夸张的说法。我明白。

cues.en: you like to see... Well, so here is the equation.
cues.zh: 你想看的是……好吧，这就是那个方程。

cues.en: This is all of everyday physics
cues.zh: 这就是日常物理的全部内容

cues.en: summarized in a single equation.
cues.zh: 用一个方程就能概括。

cues.en: I won't leave this up here for very long because there are experts in the audience looking for typos.
cues.zh: 我不会把这页放太久，因为观众里有专家在找错别字。

cues.en: But
cues.zh: 但是

cues.en: there's good news and bad news. Finding the Higgs boson was the culmination of a two thousand five hundred year quest to understand the fundamental ingredients of the world that we immediately observe.
cues.zh: 有好消息，也有坏消息。发现希格斯玻色子，是人类长达两千五百年求索历程的巅峰，它让我们理解了我们直观所见世界的根本构成。

cues.en: And we've done that. And this is one of the milestone achievements
cues.zh: 我们做到了。这也是里程碑式的成就之一

cues.en: in human intellectual
cues.zh: 在人类智力

cues.en: history and we should be very very proud and very very grateful to the people who did all the hard work.
cues.zh: 这段历史，我们应当感到非常非常自豪，也非常非常感激那些付出艰辛努力的人。

cues.en: The sad news is we know we're not done.
cues.zh: 坏消息是，我们知道我们还没做完。

cues.en: We know this is not all of physics. I'm being very very careful. This is the physics underlying the immediately accessible stuff
cues.zh: 我们知道这并不是物理学的全部。我一直在非常非常谨慎地表述。这是那些我们能直接观测的东西背后的物理学。

cues.en: of the universe. This does not tell us what happened at the Big Bang. This does not tell us why there's more matter than anti matter in the universe. It does not tell us what the dark matter of the universe is. So we need to go beyond it. We're nowhere near finished it. But if this theory
cues.zh: 宇宙的。这并没有告诉我们大爆炸时发生了什么。这并没有告诉我们为什么宇宙中的物质比反物质多。它也没有告诉我们宇宙的暗物质是什么。所以我们需要超越它。我们远未完成它。但如果这个理论

cues.en: right here fits all the data we have ever collected in every experiment here on earth, which it does,
cues.zh: 就在这儿，它拟合了我们在地球上每一项实验里收集到的全部数据，而它确实做到了，

cues.en: how do we move beyond it? We know we're not right. There are experiments outside the earth that cannot be explained by that theory. There is dark matter in the universe. This is not a simulation. This is data.
cues.zh: 我们怎样才能突破它？我们知道我们并不正确。地球之外有一些实验无法用那个理论解释。宇宙中存在暗物质。这不是模拟。这是数据。

cues.en: This is data of looking in one direction of the sky looking for the perturbations
cues.zh: 这是朝着天空一个方向观测，寻找光线传播中的扰动

cues.en: in how light travels from distant galaxies to us caused by concentrations of dark matter in the universe.
cues.zh: 这些扰动是宇宙中暗物质聚集造成的，它们会影响光线从遥远星系传播到我们这里。

cues.en: This is where the dark matter is. We know it. There's the map of it. It's not just a conjecture.
cues.zh: 暗物质就在这里。我们知道它的存在，也有它的分布图。这不只是猜想。

cues.en: We also know that the standard model of particle physics, the stuff we discovered in our laboratories cannot explain
cues.zh: 我们还知道，粒子物理学的标准模型，也就是我们在实验室里发现的那些东西，无法解释

cues.en: the dark matter. There's definitely some kind of particle, some kind of field vibrating out there and we don't yet know what it is.
cues.zh: 暗物质。那里肯定存在某种粒子，或某种正在振动的场，只是我们还不知道它是什么。

cues.en: We have ideas. We have ideas like supersymmetry and this would be a whole another hour long lecture if I were going to that. Instead, just sort of be impressed at the cuteness of this picture.
cues.zh: 我们有一些想法，比如超对称性。如果要展开讲，又得讲整整一小时。这里大家只要欣赏一下这张图有多巧妙就好。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 那么，

cues.en: supersymmetry says that for every particle we've so far discovered,
cues.zh: 超对称性认为，我们迄今发现的每一种粒子，

cues.en: there's a friend, a partner
cues.zh: 都有一个朋友，也就是一个伙伴，

cues.en: such that for every fermion we've discovered, there's a boson and for every boson we've discovered, there's a fermion.
cues.zh: 也就是说，每发现一种费米子，就有一种玻色子与之对应；每发现一种玻色子，就有一种费米子与之对应。

cues.en: So if there are if there are quarks and leptons, if there are fermions in the standard model, the rule is you put an s in the front to make the bosonic super partner, squarks and leptons.
cues.zh: 所以，如果标准模型里有夸克和轻子，也就是有费米子，那么只要在前面加个 s，就得到对应的玻色子超伙伴：s夸克和s轻子。

cues.en: Not pulling your leg here. Totally serious.
cues.zh: 我不是在逗你。完全是认真的。

cues.en: If you have a boson like gluons or gravitons, you put e no at the end. So there's glue e no's, gravity nose, etcetera.
cues.zh: 如果是胶子或引力子这样的玻色子，就在末尾加上“ino”。于是就有胶微子、引力微子，等等。

cues.en: I just found, to my shock that one of my graduate students is working on the idea that the dark matter is glueballinos.
cues.zh: 让我震惊的是，我刚发现我的一名研究生正在研究暗物质是胶球微子的可能性。

cues.en: How are you going to get respect from your parents at home when you tell them you're working on glueballino
cues.zh: 你回到家，跟父母说你在研究胶子球

cues.en: dark matter? So we're looking.
cues.zh: 暗物质，会怎么赢得他们的尊重？所以我们正在找。

cues.en: If this theory is right, there is a chance. It's not 100%. It's not 0%.
cues.zh: 如果这个理论是对的，就有机会。不是100%，也不是0%。

cues.en: There's a chance that all of these particles are findable.
cues.zh: 所有这些粒子都有可能被发现。

cues.en: The LHC,
cues.zh: 大型强子对撞机（LHC），

cues.en: is not going to find them this year because it's not running. We turned off the LHC. They are upgrading it. They are almost doubling the energy.
cues.zh: 今年是找不到它们的，因为它没在运行。我们把LHC关了，他们正在升级，能量几乎要翻倍。

cues.en: So the LHC will come back on in a couple of years in 2015
cues.zh: 所以LHC大概几年后，2015年会重新启动，

cues.en: and we are going to be looking for all of these particles and if we find them then the world will change by quite a bit.
cues.zh: 到时我们会去找所有这些粒子，如果找到了，世界会有相当大的改变。

cues.en: But we're not stopping at that. So we have here at Fermilab projects to move forward, try to discover some of these new effects. The Tevatron, the energy frontier
cues.zh: 但我们不会止步于此。费米实验室有推进项目，试图发现一些新效应。Tevatron，费米实验室项目中的能量前沿

cues.en: part of Fermilab's program has shut down but there is the intensity
cues.zh: 部分已经关闭了，但还有强度

cues.en: frontier.
cues.zh: 前沿。

cues.en: The idea that rather than doing that obvious thing of going to higher energies,
cues.zh: 这个想法是，与其去做那种显而易见的事——冲向更高能量，

cues.en: we do the subtle and precise thing of going to smaller effects,
cues.zh: 不如做那种微妙而精确的事——去研究更小的效应，

cues.en: more delicate work, looking for tiny little things that can still be just as educational
cues.zh: 更精细的工作，寻找微小的东西，它们同样能带来启发

cues.en: in terms of finding new physics.
cues.zh: 在发现新物理方面。

cues.en: So at the edge of Fermilab, don't know if you've ever noticed, there's a sign that says Welcome to Batavia City of Energy.
cues.zh: 所以在费米实验室边上，不知道你们注意过没有，有个牌子写着“欢迎来到巴达维亚，能量之城”。

cues.en: And that will be replaced with City of Intensity,
cues.zh: 那会被换成“强度之城”，

cues.en: I think totally works, branding wise.
cues.zh: 我觉得从品牌角度完全说得通。

cues.en: So this is a multi pronged program. I'm not the world's expert. I'm not going to tell you about every prong of it. I picked out my two favorite examples because I think they're kind of cool. They're all kind of cool. These are my two favorites. One of them is called the muon g minus two experiment, again because particle physicists have some special genius for coming up with names for things.
cues.zh: 这是一个多管齐下的计划。我不是世界级专家。我不会讲它的每一个方向。我挑了两个最喜欢的例子，因为我觉得它们挺酷的。它们都挺酷的。这两个是我最喜欢的。其中一个叫 μ子 g-2 实验，还是因为粒子物理学家给东西起名字特别有天赋。

cues.en: What does that mean, the muon g minus two experiment? Well, the muon is the elementary particle, the heavier partner of the electron.
cues.zh: μ子 g-2 实验是什么意思？μ子是一种基本粒子，是电子更重的搭档。

cues.en: It has a magnetic field. It's like a little spinning top,
cues.zh: 它有磁场。它像一个小陀螺，

cues.en: that with... That has an electric charge. So it has a magnetic field. It turns out that if it were just a single classical particle,
cues.zh: 它带有……它带电荷。所以它有磁场。结果发现，如果它只是一个经典粒子，

cues.en: there's a number called g
cues.zh: 有一个叫 g 的数

cues.en: which tells you the shape of the magnetic field around the particle and if it were classical, g would be equal to two.
cues.zh: 它告诉你粒子周围磁场的形状；如果它是经典粒子，g 会等于 2。

cues.en: But it's not. The muon is a vibrating quantum field. So when that muon vibrates,
cues.zh: 但并不是。μ子是一个振动的量子场。所以当 μ子振动时，

cues.en: it gently shakes all of the other fields next to it. Now we are trained from birth to think of particles,
cues.zh: 它会轻轻摇动旁边所有其他场。我们从小就被训练成用粒子来思考，

cues.en: not fields. So what we think of are not vibrating fields,
cues.zh: 而不是场。所以我们想到的不是振动的场，

cues.en: but virtual
cues.zh: 而是虚

cues.en: particles.
cues.zh: 粒子。

cues.en: So physicists think about the muon being surrounded by a buzzing cloud of virtual particles, which are not other muons, they're any particles
cues.zh: 所以物理学家认为 μ子被一团嗡嗡作响的虚粒子云包围着，这些不是别的 μ子，而是任何粒子

cues.en: that could couple to photons and muons and so forth. And it's the combination of all this buzzing cloud of virtual vibrating fields that gives rise to the true
cues.zh: 只要它们能与光子、μ子等耦合。正是这整团嗡嗡作响的虚振动场组合起来，才产生了真正的

cues.en: magnetic field of the muon.
cues.zh: μ子的磁场。
